newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices steady to up despite crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices steady to up despite crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to higher Thursday in thin trade, with tight stocks underpinning the complex despite softer crude and mild weather that has killed utility demand, industry sources said.
"Things are slow with the (mild) weather, but (prompt) stocks are still relatively tight. People are hyping resid up," said one cash trader.

At the U.S. Gulf Coast, three percent firmed a quarter to $16.75 or better on reports 40,000 prompt barrels sold at $17.25 (FOB Baton Rouge). USG one percent held relatively steady near the $17 level, traders said.

In New York Harbor, prompt one percent was unchanged at $18.50-75 a barrel, with October paper pegged early at about $19 but likely lower later with crude. Early quotes for NYH November one percent paper were in the $19.20 area.
Traders said 40,000 barrels of prompt one percent were done at $18.90 (delivered Baltimore).
With gas still cheap and mild weather forecast into next week, few expected much upside in resid near-term, but they said at some point, prices could firm as utilities begin stocking for winter.
New York city gate swing gas prices gained five to 10 cents on the day to the $2.10-2.15/mmBtu level versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.96/mmBtu equivalent.
